title-missing.title: Page title missing
title-missing.why: The page title is the blue headline in search results and the text in the browser tab. Without one, Google invents a title from the page, often badly, and the page is much less likely to be clicked.
title-missing.fix: Open the page in Umbraco (in the right language) and fill in its title. Many sites have a separate SEO or meta title field, usually on an SEO tab; if the field is empty the site's template should fall back to the page name. If the page has a name and still no title, ask a developer to check the template.

title-length.title: Page title too short or too long
title-length.why: Google shows roughly 50–60 characters of a title. Longer titles are cut off with "…", so the end of the title — often the part that sets the page apart — is lost. Very short titles waste the most visible spot in the search result.
title-length.fix: Aim for 30–60 characters: what the page is about first, the site name last if at all. Edit the page's title (or SEO title) field in Umbraco.
title-length.caveats: Long titles aren't penalised; they're just cut off. Google may also rewrite titles it finds unhelpful. A site name appended by the template counts towards the length.

title-duplicate.title: Same title on several pages
title-duplicate.why: When several pages share a title, searchers can't tell them apart in the results, and Google has a harder time choosing which page to show.
title-duplicate.fix: Give each page a title that describes what is unique about it. Edit the title (or SEO title) field of the pages listed.
title-duplicate.caveats: Paged lists and filtered views often share titles on purpose; ignore them here if they are not meant to be found on their own.

description-missing.title: Meta description missing
description-missing.why: The meta description is often used as the grey text under the title in search results. Without one, Google picks a snippet from the page, which may not make anyone want to click.
description-missing.fix: Open the page in Umbraco and write a meta description — usually on an SEO tab — of one or two sentences that say what the visitor will find and why it is worth the click.
description-missing.caveats: Google decides per search whether to use your description, so it won't always show. It doesn't affect ranking directly, only how many people click.

description-length.title: Meta description too short or too long
description-length.why: Descriptions longer than about 160 characters get cut off; very short ones give searchers too little reason to click.
description-length.fix: Aim for 70–160 characters: a clear summary of the page with the most important words early. Edit the meta description field on the page in Umbraco.
description-length.caveats: Google measures in pixels, not characters, and shortens snippets on mobile, so treat the range as a guide.

description-duplicate.title: Same meta description on several pages
description-duplicate.why: Identical descriptions make different pages look the same in search results, and Google tends to ignore them and write its own.
description-duplicate.fix: Write a description for each page that says what is specific to that page. If the template fills in a site-wide default, prefer leaving it empty over repeating it.

h1-missing.title: Main heading (H1) missing
h1-missing.why: The H1 is the page's main heading. It tells visitors and search engines what the page is about, and its absence often means the page's topic isn't stated anywhere prominent.
h1-missing.fix: Make sure the page has one visible main heading. If the page's heading field is filled in and there is still no H1, ask a developer to check the template.
h1-missing.caveats: A missing H1 isn't a ranking penalty in itself; it's a signal that the page lacks a clear topic.

h1-multiple.title: More than one main heading (H1)
h1-multiple.why: Several H1s on one page blur what the page is mainly about. It usually comes from a block or rich-text heading set to H1 in addition to the page heading.
h1-multiple.fix: Keep one H1 for the page's main heading and change the others to H2 — in the rich-text editor's format menu, or in the block's heading level setting.
h1-multiple.caveats: Google handles multiple H1s, so this is a tidiness issue more than a ranking issue.

thin-content.title: Little text on the page
thin-content.why: Pages with very little text give search engines little to understand and rank, and rarely answer a searcher's question well.
thin-content.fix: Add useful text that answers what a visitor to this page wants to know. If the page is a navigation or contact page that is fine as it is, ignore it here.
thin-content.caveats: Word count is a rough signal, not a rule. Text inside images, PDFs or content loaded by JavaScript isn't counted.

broken-internal-link.title: Broken links to the site's own pages
broken-internal-link.why: Links that lead to an error page frustrate visitors and waste the attention search engines spend on the site.
broken-internal-link.fix: Open the page in Umbraco and update or remove the links listed. Links made with the content picker follow pages when they move; typed URLs don't. Links to media files break when the file is deleted.
broken-internal-link.caveats: Only links to the site's own hosts are checked. A link to an unpublished page also counts as broken for visitors.

redirected-internal-link.title: Links that go through a redirect
redirected-internal-link.why: Each redirect adds a delay for visitors and an extra step for search engines. They usually come from links typed by hand to an old address.
redirected-internal-link.fix: Point the links listed straight at the final address — easiest by re-picking the page with Umbraco's link picker.
redirected-internal-link.caveats: A redirect from http to https or a missing trailing slash also counts; those are usually fixed in the template or site configuration.

og-missing.title: Social sharing tags missing
og-missing.why: Open Graph tags (og:title, og:image) decide what a link looks like when it's shared on LinkedIn, Facebook, Teams or Slack. Without them the share often shows no picture and a poor title.
og-missing.fix: If the site has a share image or Open Graph fields (often on an SEO tab), fill them in. If there are no such fields, ask a developer to add og:title and og:image to the template, with a site-wide default image.
og-missing.caveats: This doesn't affect Google rankings, only how shared links look.

translation-missing.title: Page missing in some languages
translation-missing.why: When a page exists in one language but not another, visitors switching language hit a dead end, and the site is invisible for searches in that language.
translation-missing.fix: Open the page in Umbraco, switch to the missing language in the language picker, write the content and publish it.
translation-missing.caveats: Some pages are meant for one language only — ignore them here.

status-error.title: Published page doesn't load
status-error.why: The page is published in Umbraco but returns an error or doesn't answer. Search engines drop pages that keep failing, and visitors see an error.
status-error.fix: Open the page's address and look at the error. A 404 usually means a routing or URL problem; a 500 is an error in the template or code — check Umbraco's log viewer for that time.
status-error.caveats: A temporary problem during the scan also shows here; use Re-check to try again.

home-hidden.title: Home page is hidden from search engines
home-hidden.why: The site's start page tells search engines not to index it, or robots.txt blocks it. The start page is usually the most important page on the site.
home-hidden.fix: Check the start page in Umbraco for a "hide from search engines" or noindex setting and switch it off. If there is none, ask a developer to check the robots meta tag, the X-Robots-Tag header and robots.txt.

hidden-but-blocked.title: Hidden page is also blocked in robots.txt
hidden-but-blocked.why: The page says noindex, but robots.txt stops search engines from reading it — so they never see the noindex, and the address can still appear in results.
hidden-but-blocked.fix: If the page should stay out of search results, remove its rule from robots.txt and keep the noindex. robots.txt controls crawling, not indexing.

canonical-missing.title: Canonical link missing
canonical-missing.why: A canonical link tells search engines which address is the real one when the same page can be reached in several ways (with or without a slash, with tracking parameters, on several hosts).
canonical-missing.fix: Ask a developer to add <link rel="canonical"> with the page's own full address to the template.
canonical-missing.caveats: Without it Google picks a canonical itself, which usually works; the tag removes the guesswork.

canonical-mismatch.title: Canonical points somewhere else
canonical-mismatch.why: The page's canonical link names another address, another host or a page that doesn't load or is hidden. Search engines may then index the other address instead, or ignore the tag.
canonical-mismatch.fix: If the page should be found on its own address, the canonical must point at that exact address. Check the template, and any canonical override field on the page.
canonical-mismatch.caveats: A canonical to another page is right when this page is a deliberate copy (for example a print or filtered version).

hreflang-missing.title: Language versions not linked (hreflang)
hreflang-missing.why: The page exists in several languages, but doesn't tell search engines so. Without hreflang links, Google may show the wrong language to searchers.
hreflang-missing.fix: Ask a developer to output <link rel="alternate" hreflang="…"> for every published language of the page, including the page itself.

hreflang-invalid.title: Language links (hreflang) are wrong
hreflang-invalid.why: Search engines ignore hreflang links that use an invalid language code, point at a page that doesn't load, aren't returned by the other page, or don't include the page itself.
hreflang-invalid.fix: Ask a developer to check the hreflang output: valid codes such as sv or en-GB, full addresses of published pages, every language version listing all the others and itself.

hreflang-no-x-default.title: No default language (x-default)
hreflang-no-x-default.why: x-default tells search engines which version to show searchers whose language isn't one of the site's languages.
hreflang-no-x-default.fix: Ask a developer to add an hreflang="x-default" link, usually pointing at the main language or a language picker.
hreflang-no-x-default.caveats: Optional, but recommended for multilingual sites.

lang-mismatch.title: Page language not stated correctly
lang-mismatch.why: The lang attribute on <html> is missing or doesn't match the page's language in Umbraco. It helps browsers, screen readers and search engines handle the text correctly.
lang-mismatch.fix: Ask a developer to set <html lang="…"> from the page's culture in the template.

structured-data-invalid.title: Structured data can't be read
structured-data-invalid.why: A JSON-LD block on the page isn't valid JSON, so search engines ignore it — and with it any rich results it was meant to give.
structured-data-invalid.fix: Ask a developer to fix the JSON-LD output and test the page with Google's Rich Results Test. Text from editors must be escaped properly.
structured-data-invalid.caveats: Only JSON syntax is checked here, not whether the schema.org content is complete.

slow-response.title: Slow server response
slow-response.why: The server took a long time to start answering. Slow pages lose visitors and can be crawled less often.
slow-response.fix: Ask a developer to look at caching and heavy queries in the page's template and blocks. Measure again: a single slow response can be a cold start.
slow-response.caveats: Measured from the server to itself, so it shows server time, not what a visitor on a phone experiences.

heavy-html.title: Very large page
heavy-html.why: The HTML alone is very large, which slows the page down for visitors, especially on mobile.
heavy-html.fix: Ask a developer to look for inlined images or data, huge menus or repeated markup in the template.
heavy-html.caveats: Only the HTML is measured, not images, scripts or styles.

sitemap-missing-page.title: Page missing from the sitemap
sitemap-missing-page.why: The sitemap is the list of pages the site asks search engines to index. Indexable pages missing from it may be found later or not at all.
sitemap-missing-page.fix: Check whether the page is excluded by a setting (often a "hide from sitemap" checkbox). Otherwise ask a developer to check how the sitemap is built.

sitemap-bad-entry.title: Sitemap lists pages that shouldn't be there
sitemap-bad-entry.why: The sitemap lists an address that is hidden from search engines, doesn't load, or isn't a published page. That sends search engines mixed signals and wastes their visits.
sitemap-bad-entry.fix: Ask a developer to build the sitemap from published, indexable pages only, and to leave out pages marked noindex.

robots-missing.title: robots.txt missing
robots-missing.why: robots.txt tells search engines what they may crawl and where the sitemap is. Without it everything may be crawled, which is usually fine, but the sitemap can't be announced there.
robots-missing.fix: Ask a developer to add a robots.txt that allows crawling and lists the sitemap address.

sitemap-missing.title: No sitemap
sitemap-missing.why: A sitemap lists every page you want indexed, which helps search engines find new and changed pages quickly.
sitemap-missing.fix: Ask a developer to add an XML sitemap at /sitemap.xml (or list it in robots.txt), built from published, indexable pages, and submit it in Google Search Console.

https-redirect.title: http doesn't redirect to https
https-redirect.why: The site answers on unencrypted http without moving visitors to https. Browsers mark it as not secure, and the same pages exist on two addresses.
https-redirect.fix: Ask a developer or the host to redirect all http requests permanently (301) to https.

host-duplicate.title: Site answers on both www and without
host-duplicate.why: The same pages answer on both www.example.com and example.com, so search engines see two copies of the site.
host-duplicate.fix: Ask a developer or the host to redirect one of them permanently (301) to the other, and use that one in Umbraco's Culture and Hostnames.

site-hidden.title: The whole site is hidden from search engines
site-hidden.why: Every page tells search engines not to index it, or robots.txt blocks everything. That is expected on a Test or Dev environment; on the live site it is the most serious problem there is.
site-hidden.fix: On the live site: ask a developer immediately to check robots.txt, the robots meta tag and the X-Robots-Tag header. On Test or Dev: set Esatto:Seo:IntentionallyHidden to true for that environment to turn this into a notice.
site-hidden.caveats: While the whole site is hidden, the other checks still run as if pages were indexable, so content issues stay visible.
